added_claim_errors: Applies the $660 carryover for 2025 funds to this 2026 scenario; the applicable maximum is $680, making the spend-down $1,220 rather than $1,240.
Gives “March 15, 2026” as the grace deadline; the applicable maximum is March 15, 2027, and plans may provide a shorter period.
“At most $660 ... survives” and March work cannot use “the other $1,240” ignore the grace-period possibility, which can preserve the entire $1,900 for qualifying March care.
“Everything is forfeited December 31” and “$1,900 becomes $0 on January 1” overlook reimbursement of timely incurred expenses claimed during the run-out period.

reasons: A gives the correct 2026 carryover maximum and spend-down calculation, explains the alternative plan features, and distinguishes treatment timing from claim submission. B corrects the opening premise but uses the previous year's figures and dates, then makes categorical loss statements that conflict with its later grace-period caveat. Both omit the 2027 election and day-one availability of the full election; A is also unnecessarily repetitive. Arithmetic independently checks out: $1,900 − $680 = $1,220, while B's $1,240 follows from its inapplicable $660 cap.
